decisive_items: Large confluent anterior cervical osteophytes from C2–T1
response.rationale: Imaging and EGD directly show large cervical osteophytes causing extrinsic esophageal compression, explaining dysphagia, hoarseness, and tongue atrophy without intrinsic malignancy. Esophageal cancer lacks mucosal lesion evidence; squamous cell carcinoma is nonspecific without biopsy.

rejected.why: No endoscopic or biopsy evidence of esophageal malignancy; compression is extrinsic from osteophytes.
Smoking and dysphagia are nonspecific; no primary tumor or nodal histology supports squamous cell carcinoma.
